description: Bounds of the pre-translation fragment stitch. The paragraph finder sometimes leaves one written unit as several paragraphs: a line broken in the middle of a word into two boxes standing side by side, a run of such boxes down a column, or the first letters of a paragraph drawn as their own small box before the rest of it. Each piece is then a translation request of its own, and half a word or half a sentence comes back as a translation of half a word or half a sentence. This pass puts the pieces back together before the translator sees them. It runs on the page as the finder left it, so what it repairs is the finder's grouping rather than anything a later stage did. A page whose declared policy raises one of 'policy_flags' is left alone entirely: its lines are records rather than prose, and assembling records is the line structure pass's question, not this one. Three rules admit a pair, and all of them share the same two guards. The style guard is that both pieces are set in one face at one size, the face read by the name the font carries rather than by the resource id it is reachable under, because the same font is registered under a different id inside every form the page draws and an id comparison would call one typeface two. 'stitch_font_size_tolerance' is the share of the size two pieces may differ by and still be one size. The unit guard is that the join is inside a written unit rather than between two: the left piece does not end its sentence, measured by 'sentence_terminators' read over its last non-space character with any closing quotation or bracket in 'closing_marks' stripped first, and one of the two pieces is short enough by 'stitch_max_fragment_chars' to be a piece rather than a paragraph. Two full paragraphs, one ending where the next begins, are what running text looks like everywhere; without this guard the geometry alone would join a whole column into one request. Rule 'inline' is two pieces on one line: their line bands overlap by 'stitch_min_y_overlap_ratio' of the shorter band and the horizontal space between them is no wider than 'stitch_max_inline_gap_ratio' of their own type size. Rule 'vertical' is one piece above another in one column: their boxes overlap horizontally by 'stitch_min_x_overlap_ratio' of the narrower and the vertical space between them is no deeper than 'stitch_max_line_gap_ratio' of their own median height. Inline runs first and vertical runs over what inline produced, because a line has to be whole before the column below it can be read as continuing it. Rule 'initial' is the dropped initial that arrived as its own fragment: a cluster of no more than 'initial_max_chars' characters set at 'initial_min_font_ratio' times the size of the body paragraph it stands at the upper left of, within 'initial_max_offset_ratio' of that paragraph's own type size of its top left corner. It carries no style guard, because an initial is set in another face by design; it carries the unit guard, because an initial that is not the opening of the words beside it is not one. 'stitch_layout_labels' is the closed set of layout labels a piece may carry. Page furniture -- a running foot, a printing slug, a masthead drawn as separate letters -- is fragmented too, and putting it back together repairs nothing, because nothing translates it; what the stitch exists for is a broken translation unit. 'rules' is the closed vocabulary of the rule names a record may name, and 'sidecar_fields' is the shape of one stitch record, both asserted against what the pass writes so the report's form is declared here rather than implied by the code. A page whose policy raises one of policy_flags is a page whose lines are records, and B10.3 left every such page alone. That is right for the vertical rule, which joins paragraphs down a column and would join two records; it is too wide for the inline rule, which works inside one line band and by construction cannot reach across a record boundary. So declared_page_rules names the rules that may still run on such a page, and declared_page_switch names the run attribute that lets them -- a name rather than a bound, so it carries no allowed range and is read as a structural key rather than as a parameter. What they may run on is narrower still: declared_page_classes names the classes babeldoc/magazine/source_audit.py has to have placed every member of a group in before the group is stitched there, and duplicate_blank_classes names the classes whose members are blanked instead, because a layer the page holds twice wants the surplus removed and stitching it would build a paragraph saying everything twice. A fragment the audit leaves in any other class is not touched on a declared page at all. The two lists have to be disjoint: no class can mean both repair. ASCII only, as the other configuration files are: every character outside ASCII -- the Chinese sentence terminators and closing marks below -- is written as a JSON escape, so the file reads the same on any console and the gate that holds this project's declarations to ASCII has nothing to report. The parsed value is the character itself.
